Next Session includes at least two teen-number items; two unassisted first-try corrects return this to 0.85, another miss moves it to 0.55.

hypotheses.claim: The compose direction of teen numbers is weaker than the decompose direction.
hypotheses.nextTest: No compose item ran; the miss this Session was in the decompose direction (p177), which points the other way. Reopen as proposed only if two compose items miss in one Session while decompose first attempts stay correct.

hypotheses.claim: Misses arrive in runs by position rather than on particular numbers.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated refuting condition occurred: assisted items appeared in the last three positions (7 + 5 at position 9, p184; 7 + 7 at position 10, p185) as well as at positions 2, 6 and 7, so help was not confined to one part of the Session. Reopen as proposed only if a whole Session's assisted items again fall in one unbroken block of positions.

hypotheses.claim: When Unit 1 Skills are interleaved with harder Unit 2 work, Unit 1 first attempts mostly hold up.
hypotheses.nextTest: Against: both Unit 1 items were first-try misses finished after one Hint (10 + ? = 13 at position 2, p177; 10 - 8 at position 6, p181), with no Reveal. Next Session runs at least three Unit 1 items; two or more unassisted first-try corrects move this back to supported at 0.65, two or more misses again move it to refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten across ten is usually right on the first try in both structures, with occasional single misses.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated return condition was met: two of three make-a-ten first attempts missed (7 + 5, p184; 7 + 7, p185), each finished after one Hint, against one unassisted first-try correct (4 + 8, p176). Next Session keeps make-a-ten as the largest share; three or more unassisted first-try corrects move this back to supported at 0.65, two or more misses again hold it at 0.4.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten within 20 is the current weak spot: a sizeable share of first attempts miss and the item is completed only with help.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated return condition was met: two of three make-a-ten first attempts missed and were finished after a single Hint each (p184, p185), with one unassisted first-try correct (p176). Next Session runs four or more make-a-ten items; three or more unassisted first-try corrects move this toward 0.35, two or more misses again hold it at 0.7.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on first-try accuracy is inconsistent and is not explained by structure or by number size.
hypotheses.nextTest: Against: both counting-on items were unassisted first-try corrects (p178, p183). Reopen as proposed at 0.4 if two counting-on first attempts miss in one Session.

hypotheses.claim: On unknown-addend items, first attempts hold up when the given part or whole is small but not when a teen number is involved.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further against: two teen-whole items were unassisted first-try corrects (18 - 14, p179; 8 + ? = 11, p180) while the one miss also had a teen whole (15 - 14, p182). Reopen as proposed only if every teen-whole item misses in one Session while items with wholes under 10 stay first-try correct.

hypotheses.claim: Unknown-addend is a broad gap right now: first attempts miss across whole sizes and the item is only completed after a Hint or a Reveal.
hypotheses.nextTest: Against: two of three unknown-addend first attempts were correct with no assistance (p179, p180) and the single miss was finished after one Hint (p182). Reopen as proposed if three or more unknown-addend first attempts miss in one Session across both structures.

hypotheses.claim: Unknown-addend first attempts mostly hold up across the range of wholes sampled, in both the subtract and the missing-addend form.
hypotheses.nextTest: Partly met: two unassisted first-try corrects, one in each form (18 - 14, p179; 8 + ? = 11, p180), and one first-try miss finished after a Hint (15 - 14, p182). Next Session runs at least three unknown-addend items across both forms; three or more unassisted first-try corrects move this to supported at 0.65, two or more misses hold it at 0.4.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance is now sparse and shallow: roughly one or two items per Session draw help, they are scattered across different Skills, and each is answered correctly after a single Hint rather than ending in a Reveal.
hypotheses.nextTest: Half met: help was shallow again, with all five assisted items finished after a single Hint and no Reveal (p177, p181, p182, p184, p185), but five of ten items is not sparse. Reopen as proposed only if two consecutive Sessions each show two or fewer assisted items with no Reveal.

hypotheses.claim: Assisted items arrive in clusters of adjacent positions that cross Skills, rather than being spread evenly through the Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated refuting condition occurred: an assisted item sat alone between first-try corrects (10 + ? = 13 at position 2, p177, between p176 and p178), even though two other pairs were adjacent (p181 and p182; p184 and p185). Reopen as proposed only if a Session shows every assisted item adjacent to another.

hypotheses.claim: The item immediately following an assisted item tends to draw help itself, whatever its Skill.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated refuting condition occurred: two items directly after an assisted item were unassisted first-try corrects (p178 after p177; p183 after p182), while two others did draw help (p182 after p181; p185 after p184). Reopen as proposed only if three or more items following help in one Session also need help with no exceptions.

hypotheses.claim: The weak spot has shifted: unknown-addend now draws the misses while make-a-ten first attempts are correct in the same Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Clearly against: make-a-ten drew two Hints (p184, p185) while two of three unknown-addend items were unassisted first-try corrects (p179, p180). Reopen as proposed only if a Session shows every make-a-ten item first-try correct while two or more unknown-addend items need help.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, the missing-addend form draws the misses while the subtract form is first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated refuting condition occurred: the missing-addend item was an unassisted first-try correct (8 + ? = 11, p180) while the one miss was in the subtract form (15 - 14, p182). Reopen as proposed only if two missing-addend items miss in one Session while every subtract item is first-try correct.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, the larger-first structure draws the misses while smaller-first first attempts are correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated reopen condition was met: both first-try misses were larger-first and each was finished after one Hint (7 + 5, p184; 7 + 7, p185), while the smaller-first item was an unassisted first-try correct (4 + 8, p176). Next Session runs at least two items of each make-a-ten structure; two or more larger-first misses with every smaller-first item first-try correct moves this to supported at 0.6, a smaller-first miss or larger-first items first-try correct moves it back to refuted.

hypotheses.claim: When a make-a-ten item does miss on the first try, a single Hint is enough to finish it correctly, rather than the item ending in a Reveal.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated reopen condition was met: both make-a-ten first-try misses were finished correctly after a single Hint with no Reveal (p184, p185). Next Session: any further make-a-ten misses again resolved by one Hint move this to supported at 0.65, a Reveal moves it back to refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend subtract items, first attempts miss when the two numbers are close together (a small difference) and hold when the difference is larger.
hypotheses.nextTest: Slightly toward the claim: the subtract item with a difference of 1 was a first-try miss finished after one Hint (15 - 14, p182) while the difference-of-4 item was an unassisted first-try correct (18 - 14, p179); this is one instance, not the two required. Reopen as proposed at 0.4 if two close-difference subtract items miss in one Session while larger-difference subtract items stay first-try correct.

hypotheses.claim: Within take-from-ten, first attempts miss when the given partner is large and the answer is small, while items with a middling partner stay correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Toward the claim but thin: the only take-from-ten item had a large given partner and was a first-try miss finished after one Hint (10 - 8, p181). Next Session runs two take-from-ten items with a large given partner; two first-try misses move this to supported at 0.6, two unassisted first-try corrects move it to refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance has deepened: some first-try misses end in a Reveal rather than being finished after a single Hint.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated move-down condition was met: all five assisted items this Session were first-try misses finished correctly after a single Hint, with no Reveal anywhere (p177, p181, p182, p184, p185). Next Session: another Session with no Reveal moves this toward 0.2, any Reveal moves it back to supported at 0.6.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance is front-loaded within a Session: the early items draw the help while the same Skills are first-try correct later in the same Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: The stated refuting condition occurred: the last two positions both drew help (p184, p185) while position 1 was an unassisted first-try correct in the same Skill (4 + 8, p176). Reopen as proposed only if a full Session again confines all help to the first half.

hypotheses.claim: Unit 1 Skills are now the ones drawing help while Unit 2 items in the same Session are mostly first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Seen once: both Unit 1 items were first-try misses finished after one Hint (10 + ? = 13, p177; 10 - 8, p181) while counting-on and unknown-addend items around them were unassisted first-try corrects (p178, p179, p180, p183). Next Session runs at least three Unit 1 items; two or more Unit 1 misses with Unit 2 items first-try correct moves this to supported at 0.6, Unit 1 items first-try correct moves it to refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Help now clusters toward the end of the Session: the last items draw misses while the same Skill was first-try correct at the start.
hypotheses.nextTest: Seen once: positions 9 and 10 both needed a Hint (p184, p185) and position 1 in the same Skill was an unassisted first-try correct (p176), with four of the five assisted items in the second half. Next Session: the last three positions again drawing help while the first three are first-try correct moves this to supported at 0.55; the last three positions being first-try correct moves it to refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten items miss when the larger addend is 7 and hold when it is 8 or 9.
hypotheses.nextTest: Consistent with this Session: both misses had 7 as the larger addend (7 + 5, p184; 7 + 7, p185) while the item with 8 was an unassisted first-try correct (4 + 8, p176); against it, an earlier miss had 9 as the larger addend (2 + 9, p169). Next Session runs make-a-ten items across the full 6 to 9 range; two more misses with a larger addend of 6 or 7 while items with 8 or 9 stay first-try correct moves this to supported at 0.55, a miss with 8 or 9 moves it to refuted.

strengths: Counting on is solid both ways round, with 15 + 1 and 3 + 11 right first time.
Reads subtraction as a missing part confidently: 18 - 14 and 8 + ? = 11 were both right first time.
Starts a Session strongly, getting a cross-ten addition like 4 + 8 right straight away.
Uses a Hint really well: every question that went wrong this Session was finished correctly right after one Hint.
Keeps working all the way to question ten and never gives up on a hard one.
Knows a teen number is ten and some more, even when a particular one needs a nudge.

output.practiced: Your child worked on 5 strategies today. Counting on from the larger number was mastered, with 2 problems first-try correct. Subtraction as unknown addend had 2 first-try correct and 1 correct after a Hint, and make-a-ten within 20 had 1 first-try correct and 2 correct after a Hint. Partners to 10 and teen numbers each had 1 problem correct after a Hint. Nothing was revealed, nothing was left blank, and no Power was earned this time.
output.activity: Put 10 small items in an egg carton row and a few more beside it. Ask for 7 and 5 together, and let your child move items over to fill the ten first, then count what is left outside. Try 7 and 7 next.

judged.reason: Every claim matches the tally exactly, the note distinguishes first-try corrects from Hint-assisted ones and states no Reveals or Powers, makes no inferences about the child's thinking, and the activity targets make-a-ten within 20, the named weakest skill.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on is secure when the addends are small; the one item needing help was 9 + 3 (larger first addend).
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted; no counting-on item ran this Session. No further test for h1.

hypotheses.claim: Partners to 10 is reliable on first attempts in both directions (missing-partner and take-from-ten).
hypotheses.nextTest: Untested this Session (no partners-to-10 item ran), so confidence is held roughly steady. Next test: run at least one missing-partner and one take-from-ten item; a first-try miss on either would push this back to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Problems with the unknown in the middle of the equation are answered on the first try just as often as problems where the unknown is the result.
hypotheses.nextTest: Weakened this Session: of three middle-unknown items, one was first-try correct (p175, 10 + ? = 19) while two missed on the first try (p174 Reveal, 16 - ? = 12; p178 Hint, 8 + ? = 15). It is not refuted because the result-position set was not clean either (p171 Hint, 7 + 9). Next test: run at least three middle-unknown items and three result-position items in one Session; middle-unknown misses alongside a clean result-position set would refute this, a similar miss rate in both positions would keep it proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Teen-numbers compose items (10 + 6 = ?) are not yet as dependable as decompose items.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted; this Session's decompose item was first-try correct (p175). No further test for h4.

hypotheses.claim: Because partners-to-10 and teen numbers are both solid on first attempts, make-a-ten items (crossing ten) will be reachable with little or no assistance.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted overall, though two of three make-a-ten items were first-try correct this Session (p173, 6 + 6; p177, 9 + 4) with one Hint after a first-try miss (p171, 7 + 9). Tracked under h30; no further test for h5.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, items whose larger addend is 8 or 9 draw assistance, while items with a larger addend of 6 or 7 are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: a larger addend of 9 was first-try correct (p177, 9 + 4) while a larger addend of 9 in the other framing drew a Hint (p171, 7 + 9). No further test for h6.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, items written with the larger addend first draw more assistance than items written with the smaller addend first.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: both larger-first items were first-try correct (p173, p177) and the smaller-first item drew a Hint (p171). No further test for h7.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, missing-addend items are answered on the first try when the missing part is 1, but draw assistance when the missing part is 2 or more; subtract items stay first-try correct at those sizes.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: a subtract item with a missing part of 1 was first-try correct (p172, 16 - 15). No further test for h8.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance earlier in a Session is followed by less assistance on later make-a-ten items in the same Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Previously refuted, but this Session matched the pattern once: the make-a-ten Hint fell at position 2 (p171) and the two later make-a-ten items were first-try correct (p173 position 4, p177 position 8). Reopened as proposed on one Session of evidence. Next test: run three or more make-a-ten items spread across a Session; assistance appearing on later items as often as earlier ones would refute this again.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten first-try success is rising across Sessions with continued practice, regardless of how the item is written.
hypotheses.nextTest: Reopened as proposed: two of three make-a-ten items were first-try correct this Session (p173, p177) with one Hint (p171), the best make-a-ten showing in several Sessions. Next test: run at least three make-a-ten items covering both structures; two or more first-try correct again would move this to supported, half or more assisted would refute it.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten is the only Skill still drawing assistance, and its first-try success swings from Session to Session rather than holding a steady majority.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: this Session's assistance included two change-unknown items (p174 Reveal, p178 Hint) alongside one make-a-ten Hint (p171). No further test for h11.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten items that land in the last third of a Session draw more assistance than make-a-ten items that land earlier.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: the make-a-ten Hint fell at position 2 of nine (p171) while the position-8 make-a-ten item was first-try correct (p177). No further test for h12.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten is now answered on the first try without assistance across both structures and across larger addends 6 to 9, including doubles that cross ten.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted because a smaller-first item still missed on the first try and finished after a Hint (p171), even though a crossing-ten double and a larger-first item were clean (p173, p177). Tracked by h30 and h10; no further test for h13.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, items with a whole above 15 draw assistance while items with smaller wholes are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: a whole of 16 was first-try correct (p172). No further test for h14.

hypotheses.claim: The occasional remaining make-a-ten assistance falls on doubles that cross ten (7 + 7, 8 + 8) rather than on unequal addends.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: a double was first-try correct (p173, 6 + 6) while an unequal pair drew the Hint (p171, 7 + 9). No further test for h15.

hypotheses.claim: The Unit 3 Skills (result-unknown and change-unknown) are answered on the first try, because they reuse the same part-whole facts already secure in unknown-addend and make-a-ten.
hypotheses.nextTest: Dropped from supported by its own test: four Unit 3 items with wholes of 10 or more ran, and two of them missed on the first try (p174 Reveal, 16 - ? = 12; p178 Hint, 8 + ? = 15) while the two result-unknown items were clean (p170, 7 + 9; p176, 15 + 2). The split falls entirely on change-unknown, now tracked by h33. Next test: run three or more change-unknown items and two result-unknown items at wholes of 10 to 20; clean change-unknown work would restore this to supported, more change-unknown assistance would refute the Unit-wide version.

hypotheses.claim: Unit 3 performance holds up when the whole is 10 to 20 and across the add-to and add-to-change structures, not only on small wholes and the structures seen first.
hypotheses.nextTest: Half of the due test ran against it: the add-to item with a whole of 16 was first-try correct (p170) but the add-to-change item with a whole of 15 missed on the first try and finished after a Hint (p178), and a take-from-change item with a whole of 16 ended in a Reveal (p174). Next test: run two add-to-change and two take-from-change items with wholes of 10 to 20; two or more assisted would refute this, all clean would move it to supported.

hypotheses.claim: Subtraction-shaped items draw assistance when the whole is 14 or more and the answer is 4 or larger; the same shapes with smaller wholes or answers of 1 to 3 are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: a whole of 16 with an answer of 1 was first-try correct (p172, 16 - 15) while a whole of 16 with an answer of 4 ended in a Reveal (p174), matching the rule in one case and not in the other over the wider record. No further test for h18.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance lands on items in the second half of a Session regardless of Skill, while first-half items are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: assistance fell at positions 2, 5 and 9 (p171, p174, p178), spanning both halves. No further test for h19.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance is now scattered: each Session has one to three assisted items that come from different Skills and share no common item feature, rather than clustering in one Skill or one item type.
hypotheses.nextTest: Reopened as proposed: this Session's three assisted items came from two Skills and two Units (p171 make-a-ten Hint, p174 change-unknown Reveal, p178 change-unknown Hint), breaking the run of Unit-2-only assistance. Next test: run a Session drawing on five or more Skills; assisted items again spread over two or more Units would support this, assistance confined to change-unknown would refute it in favour of h33.

hypotheses.claim: Result-unknown is currently the least dependable Skill: it draws assistance on first attempts even at easy sizes, while Unit 1 and Unit 2 Skills stay first-try correct in the same Session.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: both result-unknown items were first-try correct, including a crossing-ten total (p170, 7 + 9) and a teen part (p176, 15 + 2). No further test for h21.

hypotheses.claim: The same arithmetic is answered on the first try when it appears as a Unit 1 or Unit 2 item but draws assistance when it appears as a Unit 3 result-unknown item.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted, and this Session showed the reverse on a matched pair: 7 + 9 was first-try correct as a Unit 3 add-to item (p170) and missed as a Unit 2 make-a-ten item (p171). That reverse reading is now tracked as h34. No further test for h22.

hypotheses.claim: Within result-unknown, addition-shaped items in which one part is 10 or more draw assistance, while items whose parts are both below 10 are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: a put-together item with a part of 15 was first-try correct (p176). No further test for h23.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on items written with the larger number first, when that larger number is a teen, draw assistance, while the same numbers in other framings and smaller-first counting-on items are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted; no counting-on item ran this Session. No further test for h24.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance now comes at one to three items per Session and lands on Unit 2 Skills (make-a-ten, unknown-addend, counting-on) while Unit 1 and Unit 3 items are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Refuted by its own test: two of the three assisted items were Unit 3 change-unknown (p174 Reveal, p178 Hint), which the test named as refuting evidence, while Unit 2 unknown-addend (p172) and two of three make-a-ten items (p173, p177) were first-try correct. No further test for h25.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, items written smaller-first with 5 as the first addend draw assistance, while other make-a-ten framings are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: the assisted smaller-first item had a first addend of 7 (p171). No further test for h26.

hypotheses.claim: The amount of assistance swings widely from Session to Session and is not confined to any one Skill or Unit: some Sessions have almost none, others have assistance on more than half the items, spread across Units 1, 2 and 3.
hypotheses.nextTest: Reopened on the 'not confined to one Unit' half only: assistance rose from one item to three and spanned Units 2 and 3 this Session (p171, p174, p178). The 'more than half the items' half remains unsupported. Next test: two Sessions in a row with assisted items in two or more Units would support the spread claim; assistance settling back into one Skill would refute it.

hypotheses.claim: Within change-unknown, take-from-change items (whole minus an unknown change) draw assistance, while add-to-change items are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: both change-unknown structures missed on the first try this Session (p174 take-from-change Reveal, p178 add-to-change Hint), so the structure split does not hold. Carried forward by h33; no further test for h28.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, items written smaller-first (small addend written first, crossing ten) draw assistance, while larger-first items are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Reopened as proposed on one Session: the smaller-first item drew a Hint after a first-try miss (p171) while both larger-first items were first-try correct (p173, p177). Earlier Sessions showed larger-first items assisted too (p155, p162), so this is fragile. Next test: run at least two items of each make-a-ten structure; assistance on larger-first items would refute this again.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten is the Skill that still draws assistance most often, at roughly half its items, and the misses do not sort by structure, by which addend is larger, or by doubles.
hypotheses.nextTest: Dropped from supported: the due test ran three make-a-ten items across both structures and only one was assisted (p171 Hint; p173 and p177 first-try correct), and make-a-ten was no longer the most-assisted Skill because change-unknown drew two assisted items (p174, p178). Next test: run three or more make-a-ten items again; one or zero assisted would move this toward refuted, two or more assisted would restore support.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, subtract-shaped items draw assistance on first attempts while missing-addend items are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: a third subtract item in a row was first-try correct (p172, 16 - 15). No further test for h31.

hypotheses.claim: Total assistance per Session is shrinking: recent Sessions have at most one to three assisted items, and the remaining ones are make-a-ten.
hypotheses.nextTest: Refuted on the second half by its own test: assistance appeared outside make-a-ten this Session (p174 Reveal and p178 Hint, both change-unknown), and the count rose from one to three. Volume is still within one to three, which is now folded into h33 and h20. No further test for h32.

hypotheses.claim: Change-unknown is now the Skill drawing assistance: items with the change unknown and a whole in the teens miss on the first try in both structures, while result-unknown and unknown-addend items at the same sizes are first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Seen once: take-from-change with a whole of 16 ended in a Reveal (p174) and add-to-change with a whole of 15 finished after a Hint (p178), while result-unknown at wholes of 16 and 17 (p170, p176) and unknown-addend at a whole of 16 (p172) were first-try correct. Earlier change-unknown items at wholes of 19 and 20 had been clean (p159, p167). Next test: run three change-unknown items at wholes of 10 to 20 across both structures alongside two result-unknown items; two or more assisted change-unknown items with clean result-unknown work would move this to supported, all change-unknown items first-try correct would refute it.

hypotheses.claim: The same crossing-ten sum is answered on the first try when it is framed as a Unit 3 story total but misses when it is framed as a make-a-ten item.
hypotheses.nextTest: Seen once, on a matched pair in the same Session: 7 + 9 was first-try correct as an add-to result-unknown item at position 1 (p170) and missed, then finished after a Hint, as a smaller-first make-a-ten item at position 2 (p171). Next test: run make-a-ten items and result-unknown add-to items with the same crossing-ten sums in one Session; a repeat of the same one-way split would support this, a clean make-a-ten item at a sum already answered as a story would refute it.

strengths: Knows the partners-of-ten and take-from-ten facts and answers them right away on the first try.
Builds and breaks apart teen numbers accurately in both directions.
Counts on accurately in both framings, including when a teen number is written second.
Finds totals and results reliably, including sums that cross ten and teen-sized parts.
Subtraction as an unknown addend is dependable, including wholes in the teens and a missing part of 1.
Getting stronger at crossing-ten addition: most make-a-ten items this Session were right on the first try, including a double and a 9-plus item.
Uses a hint well: after one nudge, finishes the problem correctly.
Stays with a whole session and keeps working even after a problem has to be shown.

output.practiced: Your child worked across 5 strategies in 9 problems. output.activity: Put 10 small items in an egg carton row and a few more beside it, say 9 and 4. Ask your child to move pieces until one group is exactly 10, then say the total out loud. Swap who sets it up and do 3 rounds.

hypotheses.claim: Composing a ten and a small number (10 + n = ?) is secure across the whole range of addends, including larger addends like 7.
hypotheses.nextTest: Supported again: the Review Problem p173 (10 + 7) was first-try correct. Keep an occasional compose Problem; a first-try miss returns this to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Decomposing a teen number into 10 and some ones (10 + ? = teen) is as secure on first attempts as composing was.
hypotheses.nextTest: Untested this Session (only a compose Problem, p173, was asked). Check occasionally; a first-try miss returns this to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Partners to 10 is reliable in both structures and with both small and large given partners.
hypotheses.nextTest: Supported again: p180 (10 - 6, take-from-ten) was first-try correct, a third clean take-from-ten in a row. Keep one partners-to-10 Problem per Session; an assisted first attempt returns this to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Unit 1 Problems draw no assistance; all assistance events now come from Unit 2 Problems.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: assistance this Session fell on Unit 2 (p177, p178) and Unit 3 (p175, p179, p181). No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Difficulty in Unit 2 will concentrate on make-a-ten, because it is the Skill that requires both secure Unit 1 pieces inside one Problem; counting-on and unknown-addend will stay clean.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: this Session make-a-ten was Hint-assisted (p178) but counting-on was also revealed (p177), while unknown-addend was clean (p176). No further test planned; make-a-ten's own reliability is tracked by h42.

hypotheses.claim: Counting on from the larger number is not yet steady; it needs re-testing rather than being treated as done.
hypotheses.nextTest: Moved to supported by the pre-registered condition: p177 (3 + 11) was revealed, a second heavy assistance event on this Skill in two Sessions, though p174 (1 + 9) was clean. Next Session asks two counting-on Problems; two clean first attempts return this to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Unknown-addend success depends on the size of the missing part: small missing parts (1-2) draw assistance while missing parts of 3-5 come out clean.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: p176 (missing part 5) was first-try correct while earlier parts of 1 and 5 split both ways. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In unknown-addend, Problems whose whole is above ten draw assistance, while wholes of ten or less are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: p176 (whole 11) was first-try correct. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Within make-a-ten, the Hints come on the bigger crossings (larger addend 8-9) rather than the smaller ones (larger addend 5-7).
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: p178 (4 + 7, larger addend 7) was Hint-assisted. No separate test; make-a-ten reliability is tracked by h42.

hypotheses.claim: In counting-on, assistance comes when the smaller addend is stated first (smaller-first), while larger-first orderings are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Weakened: both counting-on Problems this Session were smaller-first and they split (p174 clean, p177 revealed), so structure alone did not sort them. Next Session asks a larger-first Problem with a teen larger addend; assistance there refutes this.

hypotheses.claim: In unknown-addend, assistance appears only when the whole is in the teens and the missing part is 3 or more; teens wholes with a missing part of 1-2, and all wholes of ten or less, are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: p176 (whole 11, part 5) was first-try correct. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In the subtract form of unknown-addend, assistance appears when the amount taken away is 10 or more (so the two parts are very unequal), while subtracting a single-digit part is answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted; p176 (11 - 6) was clean and is consistent with the refutation. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Unit 1 Skills lose their first-try reliability when they are absent from the planned diet for several Sessions; bringing them back will show first-attempt misses rather than clean work.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: p173 (teen-numbers, returning after several Sessions) and p180 (partners-to-10) were both first-try correct. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In partners-to-10, assistance appears when the partner the Learner must supply is small (1-3), while a missing partner of 4 or more is answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: p180 was first-try correct with a partner of 4. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In counting-on, assistance appears when the larger addend is 10 or more (so the count runs into the teens), while single-digit larger addends are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Moved to supported by the pre-registered condition: p174 (larger addend 9) was first-try correct and p177 (larger addend 11) was revealed, the same split as p169 last Session. Next Session asks counting-on at both a single-digit and a teen larger addend again; a clean teen-addend Problem or an assisted single-digit one returns this to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance events are now sparse and scattered: one or two per Session, landing on different Skills and structures with no content feature that predicts them.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted on the sparseness clause: five of ten Problems drew assistance this Session. The successor claims about spread and severity are h39 and h40.

hypotheses.claim: The Unit 3 story structures (result-unknown, change-unknown) will be answered on the first try from the start, because the arithmetic inside them is already secure in Units 1 and 2.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: all three change-unknown Problems drew assistance this Session (p175, p181 Hints; p179 Reveal). No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Change-unknown Problems draw assistance in both of their structures, even when the numbers are small and inside ranges the Learner handles cleanly elsewhere.
hypotheses.nextTest: Supported in both structures this Session: take-from-change p175 (11 - ? = 4) and p181 (7 - ? = 2) were Hint-assisted and add-to-change p179 (2 + ? = 11) was revealed, even though p181's numbers are ones handled cleanly elsewhere. Keep both structures in the diet; a whole Session clean in both would push this back to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: In result-unknown, whether a first attempt is correct is not sorted by the size of the numbers.
hypotheses.nextTest: Supported again: p182 (10 + 2, total 12) was first-try correct. Keep one result-unknown Problem per Session with totals varied; a run of misses concentrated at large totals would push this back to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance clusters in the opening Problems of a Session, and later Problems of the same difficulty come out clean.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: positions 1 and 2 were clean (p173, p174) and assistance ran from position 3 to position 9 (p175 through p181). No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In change-unknown, first attempts come out correct when the change (the missing amount) is 1, and miss when the change is 3 or more, in both structures.
hypotheses.nextTest: Firmly refuted. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Within the Mastered Unit 2 Skills, first-attempt misses now land on Problems whose quantities run past ten, while Problems staying at ten or below are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: p178 (4 + 7, sum 11) drew a Hint but p176 (whole 11) was clean, so quantities past ten again fell on both sides. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Within change-unknown, first-attempt misses are not sorted by change size or by structure; they appear across the whole small-number range, so the Skill needs volume rather than a narrowed slice.
hypotheses.nextTest: Supported again: this Session assistance hit both structures and changes of 5, 7 and 9 at wholes of 7 and 11 (p175, p179, p181), with no clean contrast to mark off a safe slice. Next Session keeps change-unknown as the largest share with both structures and varied wholes; a Session where assisted items share one clear feature would return this to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Inside Unit 3 the difficulty is specific to solving for the change: result-unknown first attempts are clean while change-unknown keeps producing misses.
hypotheses.nextTest: Reopened from refuted: for a third Session running result-unknown was clean (p182) while every change-unknown Problem drew assistance (p175, p179, p181); the contrary case remains p163 (result-unknown Hint). Next Session asks one or two result-unknown Problems alongside change-unknown; an assisted result-unknown first attempt refutes this again.

hypotheses.claim: The same missing-addend arithmetic is answered on the first try when it is posed as a partners-to-10 Problem but draws assistance when it is posed as a change-unknown story.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted on the accumulated record; this Session the bare Problems p176 and p180 were clean and the stories were assisted, but p164 (story) was clean last Session. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: An identical Problem answered on the first try in one Session can still draw assistance when it comes back as a Review Problem later, so repeated Review items are not automatically clean.
hypotheses.nextTest: Weakened: the one Review Problem this Session, p173 (10 + 7), was first-try correct. Keep a small Review share; an assisted Review repeat would move this to supported.

hypotheses.claim: Unknown-addend first attempts have become less reliable in the last few Sessions, and the misses do not line up with whole size or missing-part size.
hypotheses.nextTest: Weakened again: only one unknown-addend Problem was asked and p176 (11 - 6) was first-try correct, a second clean one in a row. Next Session asks two unknown-addend Problems, one in each form; two clean first attempts refute this, an assisted first attempt moves it to supported.

hypotheses.claim: When change-unknown draws assistance now, a single Hint is enough to finish the Problem correctly; Reveals have stopped appearing on this Skill.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: p179 was revealed this Session, though p175 and p181 finished after one Hint. No further test planned; the severity claim is h40.

hypotheses.claim: In partners-to-10, the take-from-ten form (10 - n = ?) draws assistance while the missing-partner form (n + ? = 10) is answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Firmly refuted: take-from-ten was first-try correct three times running (p160, p172, p180). No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance now lands on Skills that get only one Problem in a Session, while Skills given several Problems in the same Session come out clean.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: single-Problem Skills split again (p178 assisted; p176, p180, p182 clean) while the three-Problem Skill change-unknown drew three assistance events. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: Change-unknown first attempts have turned reliable in both structures at wholes up to about 12.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: wholes of 7 and 11 all drew assistance this Session (p175, p179, p181). No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In unknown-addend, the missing-addend form (n + ? = whole) draws assistance while the subtract form (whole - part = ?) is answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted; p176 (subtract form) was clean, which is consistent but does not revive the claim after p168. No further test planned; unknown-addend reliability is tracked by h28.

hypotheses.claim: Within a single Session, a second Problem on the same Skill is answered on the first try, even when the first one on that Skill drew a Hint.
hypotheses.nextTest: Further refuted: after the Hint-assisted p175 the next two change-unknown Problems were also assisted (p179 Reveal, p181 Hint). No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In change-unknown, assistance now falls on the add-to-change form (n + ? = whole) while the take-from-change form (whole - ? = part) is answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Refuted by the pre-registered condition: both take-from-change Problems drew Hints (p175, p181). No further test planned; the no-sorting claim is h24.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance is now confined to change-unknown; the six Mastered Skills are answered on the first try whatever their structure or number size.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: counting-on (p177 Reveal) and make-a-ten (p178 Hint) drew assistance again. No further test planned; the successor claim is h39.

hypotheses.claim: In take-from-change stories, assistance appears when the starting whole is above ten, while wholes of ten or below are answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Firmly refuted: p181 (7 - ? = 2, whole 7) drew a Hint just as p175 (whole 11) did. No further test planned.

hypotheses.claim: In change-unknown, the take-from-change form (whole - ? = part) draws assistance while the add-to-change form (n + ? = whole) is answered on the first try.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stays refuted: the add-to-change Problem p179 was revealed this Session alongside the two assisted take-from-change Problems. No further test planned; the no-sorting claim is h24.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance is not confined to any one Skill: it reappears on Mastered Skills as well as change-unknown, and which Problems draw it varies from Session to Session rather than tracking Skill, structure, or number size.
hypotheses.nextTest: Supported for a third Session: assistance landed on counting-on (p177) and make-a-ten (p178) as well as all three change-unknown Problems, while other Mastered Skills were clean (p173, p174, p176, p180, p182). Note one partial exception to the 'no feature' clause: counting-on assistance has now twice tracked a teen larger addend (h16). Keep one Problem on each of several Mastered Skills next Session; a Session where every assisted Problem is change-unknown would return this to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Assistance is escalating in severity: Problems that draw help now often need a full Reveal rather than finishing after a single Hint.
hypotheses.nextTest: Refuted by the pre-registered condition: three of the five assisted Problems this Session finished after one Hint (p175, p178, p181) and only two were Reveals (p177, p179). No further test planned unless Reveals dominate two Sessions running.

hypotheses.claim: Add-to-change is unreliable across its whole range: assistance appears at wholes both below ten and in the teens and at changes from 1 to 6, so no slice of it is currently safe.
hypotheses.nextTest: Partly tested: only one add-to-change Problem was asked and p179 (whole 11, change 9) was revealed, extending the unreliable range to a change of 9. Next Session asks several add-to-change Problems at varied wholes; assistance at small and teen wholes alike moves this to supported, assistance confined to teen wholes refutes it.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten first attempts have become unreliable again, and the assistance does not track which addend is stated first or how large the larger addend is.
hypotheses.nextTest: New: p178 (4 + 7, smaller-first, larger addend 7) was Hint-assisted, following the revealed p167 (5 + 8) and the Hint on p157 (larger addend 7). Next Session asks two make-a-ten Problems with different larger addends and both orderings; two clean first attempts refute this, another assisted first attempt moves it to supported.

hypotheses.claim: Change-unknown is the one Skill where most first attempts still miss: nearly every change-unknown Problem in recent Sessions has needed a Hint or a Reveal.
hypotheses.nextTest: Supported: all three change-unknown Problems this Session drew assistance (p175, p179, p181), after three of four last Session. Next Session gives change-unknown the largest share; two or more clean first attempts on it would return this to proposed.

strengths: Finishes correctly after one Hint most of the time, as on p175, p178 and p181.
Knows the partners of ten in both directions, answering 10 - 6 on sight.
Composes teen numbers from ten and ones reliably, including on Review items like 10 + 7.
Handles bare subtraction as unknown addend past ten, as in 11 - 6.
Counts on comfortably when the larger number is single-digit, as in 1 + 9.
Adds within twenty in the result-unknown story form without hesitation.
Steady, unhurried pace on first attempts across every structure tried, and keeps working after a Reveal rather than stalling.

output.practiced: Your child worked across 7 strategies today. Partners to 10, teen numbers, subtraction as unknown addend, and result or total unknown were each answered first try, and counting on from the larger number had 1 first try correct and 1 where the answer was shown after a second miss. Make-a-ten within 20 took a Hint, and change unknown had 2 correct after a Hint and 1 shown. Nothing new was mastered this Session and no Power was earned. Ollie is watching whether change unknown stays hard across both its forms.
output.activity: Put 7 buttons in your hand and count them together. Hide some behind your back and show the rest, then ask how many are hiding. Swap roles and let your child hide them for you. Do it 3 or 4 times with different amounts.

judged.reason: All counts match the tally, the three evidence types (first try, after a Hint, Revealed) are kept distinct, the note makes no claims about the child's thinking, correctly reports no Mastery or Power, frames the change-unknown claim as a Hypothesis Ollie is watching, and the hidden-buttons activity targets the weakest Skill (change unknown).

practice.name: Counting on from the larger number

hypotheses.claim: Teen-number decompose problems with larger teens (16 and up) are less secure than with smaller teens.
hypotheses.nextTest: No test this Session: the decompose item was 10 + ? = 15, below the 16 to 19 band, and it was first-try correct (p173), as was compose 10 + 7 (p165). Reopen only if two or more decompose items in the 16 to 19 band draw a Hint or Reveal in one Session while a smaller teen in the same Session is first-try correct.

hypotheses.claim: Help tends to land in the closing stretch of a Session, in the last third of the Problems.
hypotheses.nextTest: Stated restore condition met: both help events were Reveals in the closing stretch (position 8, p172; position 10, p174) while positions 1 through 7 were all first-try correct (p165, p166, p167, p168, p169, p170, p171) and position 9 was clean (p173). Next Session keep length at 10 and place items of every Skill in both halves; help again confined to positions 8 to 10 raises this further, any help inside the first six positions drops it back to proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Partners to 10 is secure across both structures and across the size of the given partner.
hypotheses.nextTest: Partly toward, reopen condition unmet: two partners items ran across both structures, missing-partner 3 + ? = 10 first-try correct (p166) but take-from-ten 10 - 1 Revealed (p174), and no item used a given partner of 9. Reopen only if a Session runs two or more partners items across both structures, including a given partner of 9, and all are first-try correct.

hypotheses.claim: Addition where the total crosses ten and the addends must be combined past ten is not yet reliable.
hypotheses.nextTest: Against again: the crossing-ten double 8 + 8 was first-try correct (p168) and neither help event involved a crossing-ten addition. Reopen only if two or more crossing-ten additions draw a Hint or Reveal in one Session while additions that stay at or below ten are clean.

hypotheses.claim: Help keeps landing on items of a type and size already answered first-try correct in earlier Sessions, and it is not explained by position.
hypotheses.nextTest: Downgraded as the stated rule required: both help events sat in the closing positions (Reveal at position 8, p172; Reveal at position 10, p174) and every early Problem was first-try correct, so position covers this Session's data on its own. Next Session again spread Mastered Skills across early and late positions; an early help event on a Mastered Skill restores support, help confined to the closing positions keeps this proposed.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten is secure in both orders and at the top of its range.
hypotheses.nextTest: Still moving toward restore: the one make-a-ten item, larger-first 8 + 8, was first-try correct (p168), but the restore condition of four or more items across both orders all clean in one Session is unmet. Next Session run at least three make-a-ten items across both orders with the larger addend held to 8 or 9.

hypotheses.claim: Counting-on is the least secure of the unlocked Skills, and the trouble sits with items whose larger addend is below ten.
hypotheses.nextTest: Against: both counting-on items had larger addends below ten and both were first-try correct (7 + 1, p167; 2 + 8, p170), while help fell on change-unknown (p172) and partners-to-10 (p174). Keep refuted; the size question stays with h8.

hypotheses.claim: Within counting-on, the items that draw help are the ones with a larger addend of 8 or 9.
hypotheses.nextTest: Downgraded as the stated rule required: two counting-on items with larger addends of 7 and 8 were both first-try correct (p167, p170). Next Session run at least two counting-on items with the larger addend held to 7, 8 or 9 again; help on them restores support, a second clean Session drops this toward refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Help concentrates on items where the unknown is a part rather than the total.
hypotheses.nextTest: Mixed again: one Revealed item had the change (a part) unknown (13 + ? = 14, p172) and the other had the result unknown (10 - 1, p174), while part-unknown items 10 + ? = 12 (p171), 3 + ? = 10 (p166) and 10 + ? = 15 (p173) were first-try correct. Reopen only if all help in a Session falls on part-unknown items while total-unknown items are clean.

hypotheses.claim: Unknown-addend is the one Skill that still draws help; help now falls on some of its items while others come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Against again: the single unknown-addend item was first-try correct (10 + ? = 12, p171) while help fell on two other Skills. Reopen only if two or more unknown-addend items draw a Hint or Reveal in one Session while other Skills stay clean.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, the items that draw help are the ones whose whole is above ten.
hypotheses.nextTest: Against again: an unknown-addend item with whole 12 was first-try correct (p171). Reopen only if two or more unknown-addend items with wholes above ten draw help in one Session while a small-whole item in the same Session is clean.

hypotheses.claim: Make-a-ten items written smaller-first with 9 as the larger addend draw help, while larger-first items with 9 come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: No test: the one make-a-ten item was larger-first with larger addend 8 and was clean (p168). Reopen only if two or more smaller-first items with larger addend 9 draw help in one Session while larger-first 9 items are clean.

hypotheses.claim: Unknown-addend help is scattered rather than tied to structure or to the size of the whole: within one Session the Skill produces both first-try correct items and helped items in both structures.
hypotheses.nextTest: No test: only one unknown-addend item ran and it was clean (p171). Reopen only if help falls on some unknown-addend items while others are first-try correct in both structures with no size pattern.

hypotheses.claim: Help on make-a-ten appears only at the very top of the range, where both addends are 9 (sum 18), and not on other make-a-ten items.
hypotheses.nextTest: Unchanged: no make-a-ten help at all this Session (p168 clean), and past evidence against stands. Keep refuted.

hypotheses.claim: On make-a-ten, the written order decides whether help appears: smaller-first items draw help whatever the size of the smaller addend, and larger-first items do not.
hypotheses.nextTest: No test: only a larger-first item ran and it was clean (p168). Reopen only if two or more helped make-a-ten items in one Session are all smaller-first while larger-first items are clean.

hypotheses.claim: On make-a-ten, help lands on items whose two addends are equal (doubles), while unequal pairs come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Direct evidence against: the double 8 + 8 was first-try correct (p168). Keep refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Help now appears on only one or two isolated items per Session, scattered across Skills, sizes, structures and positions, with no single feature marking them.
hypotheses.nextTest: Half toward reopening: this Session had exactly two help events (Reveals p172, p174), meeting the ceiling once, but both sat in the closing positions rather than scattered across positions. Reopen only if a second consecutive Session returns to at most two help events.

hypotheses.claim: Within unknown-addend, help now falls on items with a small whole (below ten) while items with a whole above ten come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: No test: the one unknown-addend item had a whole of 12 and was clean (p171). Keep refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Within counting-on, the items that draw help are the ones whose larger addend is above ten.
hypotheses.nextTest: No test: no counting-on item had a larger addend above ten (p167, p170 both below ten and clean). Keep refuted.

hypotheses.claim: The Unit 3 Skills (result-unknown and change-unknown) come back with at most occasional help once the Learner has met them.
hypotheses.nextTest: Test not run at the size stated: only two Unit 3 items ran, one clean (put-together 10 + 1, p169) and one Revealed (change-unknown 13 + ? = 14, p172). Next Session run four or more Unit 3 items across both Skills; at most one help event restores support, two or more drops this lower.

hypotheses.claim: Unit 3 has been tested only in its easier corner: take-from-change is now clean, but result-unknown take-from has never run and wholes above ten have barely been tried.
hypotheses.nextTest: Retired: result-unknown take-from has run with a whole above ten and was first-try correct (13 - 2, p155). Any remaining edge is tracked by h21, h26, h28 and h32.

hypotheses.claim: Help arrives in bursts rather than at a steady rate: a Session with almost no help is followed by one where help lands on many different Skills.
hypotheses.nextTest: One instance toward reopening: five help events last Session were followed by two this Session (p172, p174). Reopen only if a near-clean Session follows a heavy one a second time.

hypotheses.claim: Help lands on items that pair a 9 with a total of exactly ten, while nearby items of the same Skills without that pairing come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Downgraded: the Revealed item was take-from-ten 10 - 1, whose whole is ten and whose answer is 9 (p174), which fits loosely, but two other items totalling exactly ten were first-try correct (3 + ? = 10, p166; 2 + 8 = 10, p170) and neither showed a given 9. Next Session run partners items across both structures with various given partners, including 9; help only on the 9-items restores support, clean 9-items drop this toward refuted.

hypotheses.claim: The rate of help has risen and is holding: about half the Problems in a Session now draw a Hint or Reveal, spread across many Skills rather than concentrated in one.
hypotheses.nextTest: Downgraded as the stated rule required: only two of ten Problems drew help, across two Skills (change-unknown p172, partners-to-10 p174), with eight first-try correct. Next Session, four or more help events across three or more Skills restores support; two or fewer again drops this toward refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Result-unknown is now the main place help lands, and it draws help even on small numbers, not only on totals past ten.
hypotheses.nextTest: Test not run at the size stated: the one result-unknown item was first-try correct (put-together 10 + 1, p169) and help fell on other Skills. Next Session run three or more result-unknown items across add-to, take-from and put-together; two or more help events restores support, one or none drops this toward refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Subtraction items whose two numbers are only one apart draw help, while subtractions with a bigger gap come back first-try correct.

Next Session run at least two items whose given numbers are one or two apart and two with a gap of four or five; help only on the narrow-gap items restores support, another split drops this toward refuted.

hypotheses.claim: Within result-unknown, the add-to structure is where help lands, while put-together items come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: No add-to item ran, so no direct test; the one put-together item was first-try correct (10 + 1, p169), consistent with the claim. Next Session run result-unknown across all three structures with at least two add-to items; help confined to add-to keeps this supported, clean add-to items or help on put-together drops it.

hypotheses.claim: Items whose total is exactly ten draw help, whatever the Skill and whichever number is unknown, while items totalling more or less than ten come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Test met and failed: two items with a total of exactly ten were first-try correct this Session (3 + ? = 10, p166; 2 + 8 = 10, p170), joining the earlier clean 4 + ? = 10 (p147), while one ten-whole item was Revealed (10 - 1, p174). Reopen only if three or more ten-total items draw help in one Session while all other items are clean.

hypotheses.claim: Within teen-numbers, decompose items draw help while compose items come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: Test met and failed at the stated condition: the decompose review 10 + ? = 15 was first-try correct (p173) alongside the clean compose review 10 + 7 (p165). Reopen only if two or more decompose items draw help in one Session while compose items in the same Session are clean.

hypotheses.claim: When help appears now it comes as a Reveal rather than a worked Hint sequence.
hypotheses.nextTest: New, from this Session: both help events were Reveals on the first try (p172, p174), following the Reveal at the end of the previous Session (p164), whereas earlier Sessions mixed Hints with Reveals. Next Session watch the form of every help event; Reveals again keep this proposed toward supported, Hint-assisted successes drop it.

hypotheses.claim: Within change-unknown, help lands on the items where the change is small (1 or 2), while items with a larger change come back first-try correct.
hypotheses.nextTest: New: the two most recent change-unknown items both had a small change and both drew help after a first-try miss (9 + ? = 11, change 2, Hint, p161; 13 + ? = 14, change 1, Reveal, p172). Next Session run three or more change-unknown items across both structures so that both small and large changes appear; help confined to changes of 1 or 2 supports this, help on a large-change item or clean small-change items drops it.
